title: High Pressure Cutoff
shortDescription: High side pressure exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription: E1 on TempStar heat pump indicates the high pressure switch tripped. In cooling mode, dirty outdoor coil. In heating mode, dirty indoor coil or restricted airflow.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant pressures can be dangerous; do not bypass switches.

causes.cause: Dirty coil (outdoor in cool, indoor in heat)

fixSteps.title: Clean coils
fixSteps.instruction: Wash outdoor coil; replace indoor filter.

title: Low Pressure / Loss of Charge
shortDescription: Suction pressure or loss of charge sensor tripped.
fullDescription: E2 indicates loss of charge or low suction pressure. Common in winter heat pump operation if outdoor coil is iced over.

title: Reversing Valve Fault
shortDescription: Reversing valve did not change position.
fullDescription: E3 means the reversing valve solenoid energized but the valve did not switch, or the valve is not behaving correctly per pressure/temperature feedback.
symptoms: Heats when set to cool or vice versa

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 24V at coil and proper resistance.

faq.a: Less than other components but possible.

title: Defrost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor coil sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: E4 indicates the defrost coil sensor (thermistor) is reading invalid. Without it, the unit cannot trigger defrost properly.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip-on sensor on liquid line; swap with OEM.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E5 means the outdoor ambient sensor is open or shorted. This sensor is used for defrost timing and aux heat staging.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Match resistance curve at known temp.

title: Defrost Lockout
fullDescription: E6 indicates the heat pump entered defrost but did not clear ice within the allowed time. Could be sensor, valve, or low charge.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil
fixSteps.instruction: Allow ice to thaw fully before testing.

title: Outdoor Fan Fault
fullDescription: E7 means the outdoor fan failed to start or is below speed. Capacitor or motor most often.

title: Compressor Fault
fullDescription: E8 indicates compressor amp draw, voltage, or temperature is out of range. Could be hard start failure, capacitor, or compressor itself.

fixSteps.title: Test contactor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify pulls in and contacts not pitted.

title: Low Voltage / 24V Issue
fullDescription: E9 means the 24V transformer output is too low or too high. Could be transformer, blown fuse, or short on R-C circuit.

fixSteps.title: Check stat wire
fixSteps.instruction: Look for damage at outdoor unit.

faq.a: Often blown by stat wire short.

title: Control Board Fault
fullDescription: E0 indicates the outdoor unit control board has detected an internal fault. Power cycle may clear; if not, replacement is needed.

title: Reversing valve fault
fullDescription: Reversing valve solenoid fault. Common diagnostic code on TempStar heat pump. Resolve by following manufacturer service procedure for the implicated subsystem.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power for 10 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the implicated component, wiring, and connectors.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Test sensor with multimeter or replace if reading abnormal.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Restore power, clear codes, run system to verify.

whenToCallPro: Gas-appliance work usually requires licensed HVAC tech.

faq.a: Resolve before continued use to prevent damage or safety hazard.
